_doc: The general store and grocer (#858; the building lab's step 2). Format 1 (../FORMAT.md). valley.json town.north 'general_store' (x -54.3..-37.4, 55 x 56 ft): a two-storey false front on queen-post trusses over a goods cellar, the shop across the ground floor, a storeroom behind it, the stock loft over the shop and the family's rooms over the storeroom. Frame from saloon B's (#848), rules from the doctor's (#824-#826). Written by experiments/building_lab/store/gen_spec.py.

identity.owner: the storekeeper, a merchant who freighted his stock in from the railhead, with his wife and two children
identity.trade: a general store and grocer: dry goods, groceries, hardware, patent medicines, a post office pigeonhole counter; credit on the book
identity.means: the best-stocked building on the street: sawn lumber in 1880, painted buff with green trim, a loading dock at wagon height
identity.age_and_repair: two years: the paint fresh, the dock's boards already worn along the wagons' line, the cellar doors' hinges rust-stained
clues: the day-book open on the counter
a rolling ladder on the shelves
barrels of crackers and pickles by the stove
the scale on the post office counter

lot._doc: valley.json town.north 'general_store' (x -54.3..-37.4, depth 20): its origin the EAST front corner 3 cm off the store alley's line (x -37.4: the siding's face is the lot's line, the alley 1.2 m), west to the hardware store 14 cm off its wall. The dock and its steps are the valley's walk (h 1.1, awning 3.0, the east end dropping into the alley).

pad._doc: valley.json's pad: the lot dug level at the walk's street edge's ground (world 0.52, the building's y 0); the ground rises 0.63 m to the back of the lot

levels._doc: The floor at the loading dock's top, 1.10 m (wagon-bed height); 12 ft storeys (stock to the ceiling, a rolling ladder), 9 ft 6 in upstairs; the roof a low 2/12 on queen-post trusses (the saloon's), its ridge hidden behind the false front.

girders._doc: Lines under the ground floor's joists, a joist span 3 m; in the cellar on its posts every 1.9 m, outside it on piers.

cellar._doc: Under the front half, 13 x 9.5 m (the valley's 13 x 9): rubble-stone walls, 2.5 m under the floor. The trap by the east counter, its stair down the east wall; the doors under the dock at the street are the valley's (bulkhead: #695).

beams._doc: carries the loft's joists both sides, butted to the shop's back wall
the stair's well: the upper hall's edge beside the stair

floors._doc: the stock loft over the shop, 3x12 at 12 in across the building, broken over the two beams; the stair arrives at its back edge
the hall and the family's rooms over the storeroom, to the stair's beam

openings._doc: the recessed entry: the door 1.2 m in, glazed, a transom light over it; the show glass angling in from the posts to its jambs over a panelled bulkhead; a boarded ceiling at the head
the east show window, its display shelf behind
the stock loft's, over the show window, centred
the shop, by the east counter

walls._doc: against the hardware store (valley.json gap_n3, 0.3 m): a blank wall, no window or door

openings._doc: the storeroom's back door onto the yard, 5 steps down

walls._doc: the shop's back wall; the two bearing lines' beams butt it
the loft's back wall from the stair's corner east: the stair lands in the loft's north-east corner, the door to the hall is at x 3.0

stairs._doc: the storeroom's stair up the alley wall to the upper hall: 22 risers of 7 in, 10 in treads (Hodgson 1884)
the storeroom's back door: six steps to the yard

rooms.use: the long shop: a counter along each side, shelving to the ceiling, the stove, the scale, the post office pigeonholes; customers browse and queue, the storekeeper serves and writes his day-book
stock and the back door; the stair up to the family's rooms
the goods cellar: flour, salt pork, pickles, a keg of powder; its stair behind the east counter, its doors under the dock
stock loft over the shop: cloth, boots, hardware; windows over Main Street
the upper hall at the stair's head
the storekeeper's and his wife's bedroom
the family's sitting room and table
the children's room, or a lodger's

use_points._doc: behind the east counter (G1, #1139: its counter at x 2.0-2.6, z 2.0-5.3, in the light of the alley windows)
the day-book on the back counter; the witness's place (OUTLINE: the handsaw sold to a stranger)
the pigeonholes bay, west_shelves_d (G3, #1182: the case of pigeonholes; the postmaster's desk behind him at the back wall)
the middle front window over Main Street

ceilings._doc: #1053 (Sean's pick B on #1052): beaded boards nailed up under the loft's joists over the shop (the storeroom open to its joists: its stair goes up through them), painted pale (materials.finishes.ceiling), butted to the beams that hang under them; four beads a board

dressing._doc: #1074 the show windows' goods, #1139 batch G1 (the counters, wall shelving and ladders, the stove and its chairs, the barrels, sacks, scales and bolts of cloth), #1172 batch G2 (the shelves' tins and boxes, boots, hats, hardware, tinware, the coffee mill and a showcase, hung lamps), #1182 batch G3 (the post office's pigeonholes and mail, the postmaster's desk, the ledger and day-book, the till's cash, hung pails, hams and lanterns): PropDressing, written by tools/props/store_g1.py, store_g2.py and store_g3.py

windows.use: the east window's display platform (the glass's foot is 0.61 over the floor)
a cracker barrel, its top half over the bulkhead

G1.use: the shop's stove (the use point 'stove' stands 1.4 m in front of it)
a display table of dry goods, off the browse and buy points

light._doc: the doctor's light (#824, #829) scaled for a room 16.8 x 10.7 m: more fill and window light than his 8 m office, less than saloon B's 22 m hall; judged by day in #1035 (the doctor's 0.1 and 7 left the shop near black): 0.55 and 26

wear._why: #901: a busy store, a wagon's freight rolled in daily; dents off with the doctor's (Sean 2026-11-14)

exterior._why: Sean 2026-11-16: painted pale buff clapboard, the sheet; the merchant's pride, two years old

ceiling._why: #1053: beaded boards painted pale under the loft's joists, the doctor's ceiling; the shop read black overhead (#1052)

floor._why: oiled fir, worn on his ways (door to counter, counter to shelf), never a wall's or the trim's (#825)

timber._why: Sean 2026-11-18 (#1067): the shop's posts and beams painted pale, like the ceiling

joists._why: the floor joists stay dark: hidden over the shop's ceiling, bare over the storeroom

sources: Saloon B's frame (#848): queen-post trusses, 3x12 joists broken over girders on posts, the stacked-opening rules.
William E. Bell, Carpentry Made Easy (1858), and George Woodward, Woodward's Country Homes (1865): the balloon frame, the false front's bracing.
Hodgson, Steel Square and its Uses (1884): the stair's rise and going.
